paper.title_en: Surface-muon production for ultraslow-muon sources of $μ^+$-based colliders
paper.abstract_en: Anti-muon colliders based on ultraslow muons, such as $μ$TRISTAN and the $μ^+p$ collider LH$μ$C, need muon intensities well beyond those of present facilities. We study surface-\mup production by 3~GeV protons in graphite, molybdenum and tungsten targets with Geant4, for single, tilted and multi-layer target geometries. As single targets, molybdenum and tungsten give comparable yields, more than twice that of graphite, because a larger fraction of the beam interacts. Tilting a target with respect to a narrow beam and splitting it into several layers both raise the yield substantially: five-layer Mo and W targets give 6--8 times the surface-muon yield quoted for the J-PARC MLF graphite target, counted at the production target before capture and transport.
